evidence: Reviewed CHECK_NAME/MOVE_FILE signatures and RD/FR wildcard direction contract; authored memory/directory, failure, ordering, linkage and persistence tests; no native file-device execution

sources.topic: CHECK_NAME(name,status) checks file/program base names for illegal characters, without extensions or special system names
MOVE_FILE(file_spec,status) swaps RAM and FROM files; filename/type star wildcard forms and RD device spelling

implemented.names: Context-free portable 1..36 ASCII letter/digit/underscore base-name validation with status 0/2
implemented.movement: MemoryFiles explicit RD/FR logical names and DirectoryFiles explicit peer mappings; preserve bytes, case, suffix and literal relative subdirectory
implemented.selection: Case-insensitive star and question patterns, including explicit directory components and directory globstar. Optional single device-root separator. Bounded scans and sorted selection.
implemented.preparation: Validate rooted/symlink-safe paths, complete batch busy/collision/duplicate/size conditions before moves, including case and MemoryFiles device aliases
implemented.execution: Charge scan, move and rooted payload work before ordered backend renames. Check source metadata when refreshing the rooted byte cache. Retain completed moves on late failure.
implemented.observations: file_management_policy and ordinary value-free source/runtime service records; file snapshots retain moved bytes

portable_choices: Simple-name character/length grammar and 0/2 status are authored choices; not every native filename/program-name rule
MOVE_FILE requires explicit RD/FR context rather than controller discovery or a default device
Selected subdirectories are preserved under the peer mapping. Target parents must exist.
Move statuses 0 success, 1 source absent, 2 collision, 3 busy, 4 unmapped/unsupported/identical roots; no native alarm mapping
Budget failures precede the first rename. Later OS or status failures retain completed per-file moves without retry or rollback.
Context file data persists as logical bytes; host DirectoryFiles roots/mappings and FILE handles are not restored
remaining: Other device families and hardware metadata
